overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation on the untimely-minutes complaint, since the February minutes were approved the next month and the March and April minutes were within one to two months of the complaint; the wetlands notice claim was declined.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Commission failed to create and approve minutes of four meetings (Feb 8, Feb 22, Mar 22, Apr 8) in a timely manner.
allegations.key_passage: Because the February 8 and 22 minutes were approved the following month, we find that Commission satisfied its obligation to approve minutes in a timely manner with respect to those minutes.

allegations.summary: The March 22 and April 8 minutes were still unapproved when the complaint was filed, so the Commission exceeded the usual timing for approval.
allegations.key_passage: we do not find a violation of the Open Meeting Law because those meetings had occurred within one to two months before the complaint was filed.

allegations.summary: Complaint also alleged the Commission failed to comply with the notice requirement of the Wetlands Protection Regulations, 310 CMR 10.04.
allegations.key_passage: Because this complaint process concerns only violations of the Open Meeting Law, we decline to review allegations of violation of any other laws.

remedy: Approve the March 22 and April 8 minutes as soon as practicable (reminder, no formal order).
remedy_passage: We remind the Commission that it must approve its March 22 and April 8 minutes as soon as is practicable.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
